sense: all round, round about a place

terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative; also an adverb
evidence: Ter. Heaut. 290–291: capillus passus, prōlixus, circum caput rejectus neglegenter
Verg. G. 2.523: dulcēs pendent circum ōscula nātī
terms.comment: All the way round a thing: circum caput, round the head. Verbs repeat it: circumīre, go round; circumdare, put round, surround; circumspicere, look round.

terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative; often an adverb
evidence: Liv. 1.4.6: ex montibus quī circā sunt
terms.comment: Round about, in the neighbourhood: often an adverb, quī circā sunt, the people round about. Of times and numbers, about (Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: circā hōram prīmam).

terms.grammar: verb, irregular (like eō), with the accusative

phrases.latin: capillus passus, prōlixus, circum caput rejectus neglegenter
phrases.english: her hair loose, long, thrown carelessly round her head

phrases.latin: intereā dulcēs pendent circum ōscula nātī
phrases.english: meanwhile his sweet children hang round his neck for kisses

phrases.latin: positōsque vernās, dītis exāmen domūs, circum renīdentīs Larīs
phrases.english: and the home-born slaves, a rich house’s swarm, seated round the gleaming household gods

phrases.latin: fonticulus in hōc, in fonte crātēr; circā sipunculī plūrēs miscent jūcundissimum murmur
phrases.english: in it a little spring, in the spring a basin; round it several little jets mingle a most pleasant murmur

phrases.latin: delphīnus occurrit, et nunc praecēdere puerum nunc sequī nunc circumīre
phrases.english: a dolphin met him, and now swam ahead of the boy, now behind him, now round him
each of them surrounds his house with open ground
